name: VPS and dev boxes
ownerWords: stop being paranoid in plan under p45, p221. these should be modeled separately, like in a doc tracking all the known vps infra risks and a duty that checks these. ... things are meant to be first written in plan -> achieved -> cleared & written on duty for maintanence only -> and valiantly persued whenever not met. JUST DO IT
goal: No risk on the infra risk page (wiki domains/ops/infra-risks, its list in duties/01a11af8-962e-773d-a19a-ee4104011987/infra-risks.json) has a Grafana alert rule firing, all 9 M1 Air runners are online, and no OOM kill hits us-metal01 or us-metal02 in 24 h outside a scope of the heavy wrapper that no fix step explains. On 10-19 oom_kills_24h took over the hold of p456, after us-metal02 had 40 OOM kills from 13:14Z to 16:52Z. On 10-20 explainedKills started naming the fix step that explains each box's kills up to a time, and oom_kills_24h counts only the kills after it (p468), because p456's fixed kills held the number at 41 for a whole day. Tell the owner only when a risk fires with no fix moving it. On 10-20 alerts_firing moved to the run detail to keep one headline and 3 more: the alert bridge already gives each firing rule routed to this chat its own triage job. On 10-27 disk_days_min and the 30-day fill rules left, after the owner answered todo t78 with "stop worrying about storage being used up" (c187); a disk that is really full still fires metal-host-disk-85, and drive wear stays on metal-host-nvme-wear-30d. On 10-31 orphan_processes joined (p661): a Mac job's Chrome driver ran 2 days on us-metal02 after its job ended and made 2,320 staging Convex failures, so each run stops the processes whose owning session ended over 1 h ago. orphan_processes_unknown stays in the run detail with one orphan_unknown line per group that names no owner (p664): since c347e146 every pi kernel and its units carry LC_PRIME_SESSION, and it reads 0.

metrics.label: Risks on the infra risk page with a Grafana rule firing
OOM kills on us-metal01 and us-metal02 in the last 24 h outside heavy scopes and after the kills a fix step explains
Processes on us-metal02 whose owning agent session ended over 1 h ago, before this run stops them

onMiss: Fix a source_error first; a gap line means the risk page names a rule Grafana lacks, so fix the page's list or the rule. Each firing line names the risk page line and its owner. For each one add one fix step with duty "<dutyId>/risks_firing" naming that risk, and steer the owner's live job on it, or start one job with rlm.create_session that lands a code change for it (in auto-sns-agent through the repo's git-workflow skill 'Ship a change', plain commit.mjs on the tip, or a sieun-pi commit), and set the step's duty, job and sessionId. A risk owned by another thread gets the ask once with the page line, and this chat's fix step tracks its land. air_runners_online under 9: read devbox_runner_up by name on obs.virev.ai and bring the missing runner back on the M1 Air. oom_kills_24h over 0: each oom line names the box, its kills outside heavy scopes, about when the last kill was and the units the user journal names. heavy_scope_kills in the run detail counts the kills inside scopes of the heavy wrapper, which hit the MemoryMax their job chose; they need no step, and the job sees its own failed run. oom_kills_24h counts only the kills after the newest until of the box in explainedKills of vps-boxes.duty.json, and oom_kills_explained in the run detail counts the kills before it, named on the box's oom_explained line with its step (p456 explains every us-metal02 kill up to 16:52Z on 10-19). When a fix step lands for a new kill, add {box, until, step} to explainedKills with the time of the last kill it explains and release the file, so the fixed cause stops holding the number. Never add an entry for a kill no step fixed. For a newer kill, find the victim with journalctl --user ("killed by the OOM killer" and "oom-kill" lines) and the memory pressure around it, and add one fix step with duty "<dutyId>/oom_kills_24h" naming the box and the victim. A us-metal01 kill gets its step with the metal box owner's job (thread 01a11d24-ac9b-757d-ac51-9b2b7598782f), and a us-metal02 kill is this chat's own: stop the process with no live owner or steer the job that runs it. A line that cites /proc/vmstat means Prometheus lost node_vmstat_oom_kill, so the count runs since boot; fix the exporter first. An unchecked line is a risk with no rule; give it a rule through the Grafana alert code. The run detail's alerts_firing counts Grafana rules firing for this chat; the alert bridge's triage job holds each one, and a rule that fires on something that is not a fault gets fixed or deleted in grafana/alerting. orphan_processes over 0: the run already sent SIGTERM, then SIGKILL, to each process on an orphan line, so a count that stays over 0 on the next run means a process came back; find what restarts it from its orphan line and stop that at its cause. orphan_processes_unknown in the run detail over 0: each orphan_unknown line is a group whose parent left and that names no owner: no LC_PRIME_SESSION, RLM_SESSION_DIR or RLM_HARNESS_STATE_DIR in its env. Find its owner from the command and its folder, ask that chat to stop it or stop it yourself when its job ended, and if a kind of process keeps showing up untagged, make its starter pass LC_PRIME_SESSION. Never stop one only because it looks old. Tell the owner which risks fire and what fixes them. All on target: no message.
